files.lesson.md: --- order: 6 unit: chance node: [AC9M7P01 n1, AC9M7P01 n2] assumes: [AC9M6P01 n1] uses: [AC9M7N04 n2] # writing a probability as a fraction, decimal or percentage title: Sample spaces and probability summary: "The sample space lists every possible outcome. When the outcomes are equally likely, the probability of an event is favourable outcomes ÷ total outcomes; when they are not (a spinner with a bigger sector), use the sizes. The probabilities add to 1." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "A spinner is half red. Red, blue or green: three colours, so is each one a third? Spin it a thousand times and see." connection: game-spinner # data/connections/maths.yml (documentation only) app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8184 url: http://127.0.0.1:8184/index.html readySelector: ".ctally" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: chance.yml#pic-spinner, caption: "Sample space {red, blue, green}, but not equally likely: P(red) = 1/2, P(blue) = 1/4, P(green) = 1/4. They add to 1." } explainClip: query: { code: "@chance.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "List the outcomes, then share out the chance" say: "List every outcome, then share out the chance." clip: - caption: { text: "Sample space: {red, blue, green}. Every possible outcome.", say: "The sample space lists every possible outcome: red, blue, green." } - wait: 900 - caption: { text: "Not equally likely: red is half the spinner, so P(red) = 1/2.", say: "They are not equally likely. Red is half the spinner: a half." } - wait: 900 - caption: { text: "Blue and green are a quarter each. 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/4 = 1.", say: "Blue and green are a quarter each. Together they make one." } - click: Run 1000 - wait: 1400 --- **Probability** measures how likely something is, from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain). - The **sample space** is the list of every possible outcome: a coin $\{H, T\}$, a dice $\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\}$. - An **event** is one or more of those outcomes, such as "an even number". - When the outcomes are **equally likely**, $P(\text{event}) = \dfrac{\text{favourable outcomes}}{\text{total outcomes}}$. - The probabilities of all the outcomes add to 1. ## Predict: a third each? ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to P(blue) on a half-red spinner shows whether they assume the listed outcomes are equally likely." check: type: predict q: "A spinner is half red, a quarter blue and a quarter green. What is the probability of blue?" options: - "$\\tfrac{1}{4}$" - "$\\tfrac{1}{3}$" - "$\\tfrac{1}{2}$" actual: "1/4. There are three colours, but they are not equally likely: blue is a quarter of the spinner, so P(blue) = 1/4." ``` Three colours, but are they the same size? ## Run: spin it ```step stage: run insight: "Spinning a thousand times shows blue settling near a quarter, not a third: the outcomes in a sample space need not be equally likely." try: { playground: board, starter: "chance.yml#run", height: 620 } check: { type: board, text: "Run at least 1000 spins. Is the relative frequency of blue nearer $\\tfrac{1}{4}$ or $\\tfrac{1}{3}$? Was your prediction right?", when: "t >= 1000" } ``` The table lists the sample space, each outcome's probability, and what happened. When outcomes are **not** equally likely (a spinner with a bigger sector, a bag with more red counters), use the sizes or counts instead of dividing by the number of outcomes. ## Investigate: list, then count ```step stage: investigate insight: "List the sample space completely, check whether the outcomes are equally likely, then favourable ÷ total, or the sizes; the probabilities add to 1. Kai's mistake treats every listed outcome as equally likely." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "Roll a fair dice. What is the probability of an even number? Give a fraction in simplest form." answer: "1/2" form: simplest feedback: - ["3/6", "Right: simplify it."] - ["1/3", "The even numbers are 2, 4 and 6: three of six."] - ["3", "That is how many favourable outcomes. Divide by the total, 6."] explain: "Sample space {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}; even: 2, 4, 6. P = 3/6 = 1/2." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#kai" text: "Kai works out probabilities for the half-red spinner. Click the line where his reasoning goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: equally-likely-outcomes explain: "Line 3: favourable ÷ total only works when the outcomes are equally likely. Red is half the spinner: P(red) = 1/2, P(blue) = P(green) = 1/4." - check: type: answer q: "A bag has 3 red, 5 blue and 2 green counters. You take one without looking. What is $P(\\text{blue})$? Simplest form." answer: "1/2" form: simplest feedback: - ["5/10", "Right: simplify it."] - ["1/3", "Three colours, but more blue counters: count the counters, not the colours."] explain: "10 counters, 5 blue: 5/10 = 1/2." ``` ### List, then count Here is how to find a probability. ```worked \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\} :: List the sample space: every possible outcome of rolling a dice. \text{equally likely?} \;\checkmark :: A fair dice: each face has the same chance. \text{even} = \{2, 4, 6\} :: The favourable outcomes for the event. P(\text{even}) = \tfrac{3}{6} = \tfrac{1}{2} = 0.5 = 50\% :: Favourable ÷ total, in any form. P(\text{red}) = \tfrac{1}{2},\ P(\text{blue}) = P(\text{green}) = \tfrac{1}{4} :: Not equally likely: use the sizes. Check: they add to 1. ``` Now work out P(even) on a dice. ### Find the mistake Read Kai's reasoning. Is each colour the same size? ### Counters in a bag ## Modify: one change at a time ```step stage: modify insight: "One change at a time: a different event, a spinner with repeated labels, a missing probability, a percentage, then the edge cases of impossible and certain." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "Roll a fair dice. What is the probability of a number greater than 4? Simplest form." answer: "1/3" form: simplest feedback: - ["2/6", "Right: simplify it."] - ["1/6", "Greater than 4: 5 and 6, two outcomes."] explain: "{5, 6}: 2 of 6 = 1/3." - check: type: question q: "A spinner has three equal sectors labelled A, A and B. What is the sample space, and $P(A)$?" options: ["{A, B}, with P(A) = 2/3", "{A, A, B}, with P(A) = 1/3", "{A, B}, with P(A) = 1/2"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "List each different outcome once; A covers two of the three sectors.", "A and B are not equally likely: A has two sectors."] explain: "Two possible outcomes, A and B, but A covers 2 of 3 equal sectors: P(A) = 2/3." - check: type: answer q: "A spinner has $P(\\text{red}) = 0.5$ and $P(\\text{blue}) = 0.3$. The only other colour is green. What is $P(\\text{green})$?" answer: "0.2" feedback: - ["0.8", "The three must add to 1: 1 − 0.5 − 0.3."] explain: "0.5 + 0.3 + P(green) = 1, so P(green) = 0.2." - check: type: answer q: "Write $P(\\text{heads})$ for a fair coin as a percentage." answer: "50" feedback: - ["0.5", "That is the decimal. As a percentage: × 100."] explain: "1/2 = 0.5 = 50%." - check: type: question q: "Edge cases on a fair dice: $P(7)$ and $P(\\text{less than } 7)$?" options: ["0 (impossible) and 1 (certain)", "1/7 and 6/7", "0 and 6/6, which is not allowed"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "7 is not in the sample space at all.", "6/6 = 1 is fine: certain."] explain: "No 7 on the dice: probability 0. Every roll is less than 7: probability 1." ``` ### A different event Each task changes one thing. ### Repeated labels ### The missing probability ### As a percentage ### Impossible and certain ## Practise: probabilities ```step stage: practise insight: "Sample spaces and probabilities for coins, dice, bags and spinners, mixed; the equally-likely slip planted again; the review keeps comparing data fresh." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "A bag has 4 yellow and 6 purple counters. $P(\\text{yellow})$? Simplest form." answer: "2/5" form: simplest feedback: - ["4/10", "Right: simplify it."] - ["1/2", "Two colours, but not the same number of counters."] explain: "4 of 10 = 2/5." smaller: check: { type: number, q: "Just the counting: how many counters are in the bag altogether?", answer: 10, tolerance: 0, feedback: [[2, "That's the number of colours. Count the counters."]], explain: "4 yellow and 6 purple: 10 counters. Now how many are yellow?" } - check: type: answer q: "Pick a letter at random from the word MATHS. What is the probability it is a vowel? (A fraction.)" answer: "1/5" form: simplest feedback: - ["2/5", "Only A is a vowel in MATHS."] explain: "5 letters, 1 vowel (A): 1/5." - check: type: question q: "Which list is the full sample space for spinning this spinner: four equal sectors labelled 1, 2, 2, 3?" options: ["{1, 2, 3}", "{1, 2, 2, 3}", "{2}"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "List each different outcome once (2 is still twice as likely).", "1 and 3 can happen too."] explain: "The possible outcomes are 1, 2 and 3; 2 has probability 1/2, the others 1/4 each." - check: type: question q: "Review: Group A's median is 12 (range 4); Group B's is 12 (range 15). Which is right?" options: ["Same centre; B is much more spread", "B is better", "They are the same data"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Compare centre and spread, not a winner.", "Same median does not mean same data."] explain: "Equal medians, but B varies far more." ``` ### A bag ### Letters ### Sample space ### Review: comparing ## Make: design a bag ```step stage: make insight: "Designing a bag to match given probabilities reverses the lesson: from probabilities back to counts, using equivalent fractions." check: type: answer q: "Design a bag of 10 counters with $P(\\text{red}) = \\tfrac{3}{10}$ and $P(\\text{blue}) = \\tfrac{1}{2}$; the rest are green. How many green counters?" answer: "2" feedback: - ["8", "That is red and blue together. The rest are green."] - ["5", "That is blue: 1/2 of 10."] explain: "3 red, 5 blue (1/2 of 10), so 10 − 8 = 2 green. P(green) = 2/10 = 1/5." ``` Then: design a bag with $P(\text{red}) = \tfrac{1}{3}$. What is the smallest bag that works? ## Make: on paper ```step stage: make insight: "Counting equal sections on a made-up game spinner gives a probability, with the reason for counting picked at the key step." check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A board-game spinner has 8 equal sections: 1 is 'bonus', 3 are 'go back' and the rest are 'go on' (made up). What is P(go on)? Work it out on paper." steps: - ["8 equal sections, so 8 equally likely outcomes", "equal sections are equally likely, so we can count them"] - ["$8 - 1 - 3 = 4$ sections say 'go on'", "the favourable outcomes"] - ["$P(\\text{go on}) = \\tfrac{4}{8} = 0.5$", "favourable ÷ total"] picks: - step: 1 q: "Why can you count sections here?" options: ["The sections are equal in size, so each is equally likely", "There are three kinds of result, so each has chance 1/3", "Bonus is rare, so it is left out"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Three kinds of result, but they cover 1, 3 and 4 sections: not equally likely.", "Bonus is one of the 8 sections, so it counts."] answer: "0.5" answerLabel: "P(go on)" tolerance: 0.01 feedback: - ["4", "That counts the sections. Divide by the 8 sections to make a probability."] - ["0.33", "That treats bonus, go back and go on as equally likely. They have 1, 3 and 4 sections."] criteria: - "I counted all 8 sections as the total." - "I found the go on sections by taking away the others." - "I wrote the probability as favourable over total." explain: "8 − 1 − 3 = 4 sections say go on, so P = 4/8 = 0.5." ``` Do this one in your book or on paper, one step per line, before you type the number. **Also used in** - **Board games.** A designer splits a spinner so a bonus comes up about one spin in eight, then counts sections to check. - **Draws and raffles.** List every ticket first: that list is the sample space. - **Next lesson.** Predict and test: spin it and see how close the counts come. ```teacher summary: Students list sample spaces for coins, dice, bags and spinners, assign probabilities as favourable ÷ total when outcomes are equally likely and from sizes or counts when they are not, check that probabilities add to 1, and test a prediction with 1000 spins (AC9M7P01, nodes 1 and 2). time: 45 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 12 min · Modify 12 min · Practise and Make 13 min goals: - I can list the sample space for a single event. - I can work out a probability as a fraction, decimal or percentage. - I can tell when outcomes are not equally likely, and use sizes or counts instead. struggle: "Treating every listed outcome as equally likely (three colours, so one third each). Ask: are the sections the same size? Count equal parts, not names." before: > Do the Run board first. Students need fractions, decimals and percentages (Number Foundations). This is a hinge: everything in Chance builds on a complete sample space and correct probabilities. The common mistake is treating every listed outcome as equally likely (three colours, so 1/3 each); it is planted in the Predict and in Kai's reasoning. The board's random spins are different every time; with 1000 or more spins the relative frequencies are reliably close to the probabilities. running: - "Predict: take a show of hands; ask students who chose 1/3 how they decided." - "Run: ask what relative frequency you would expect if each colour really were 1/3." - "Investigate: write the sample space for each device on the board before any probability." - "Modify: for repeated labels, draw the spinner with A, A, B." - "Make: ask for the smallest bag with P(red) = 1/3." - "Paper: the game-spinner question is worked on paper; the page marks the number and the reason for counting sections, then shows a model. Books out, and look at the pages." stuck: - see: A student gives each colour 1/3 (Kai's mistake). ask: Is each colour the same size? fix: "Use the sizes: half the spinner is 1/2." - see: A student counts colours instead of counters. ask: How many counters are there in total? fix: Favourable counters ÷ total counters. - see: A student gives the count instead of the probability (3 instead of 1/2). ask: Out of how many? fix: Divide by the total number of outcomes. stretch: Design a spinner with four colours where one colour is three times as likely as each of the others. support: List the sample space in a table with a probability column; check the column adds to 1. leads: > Next: Predict and test (AC9M7P01 node 3, AC9M7P02 node 1): expected counts and experiments. Where it leads: complementary events and two-step experiments (Year 8). exit: q: A bag has 2 red, 3 green and 5 yellow counters. List the sample space and give each probability. a: "{red, green, yellow}: P(red) = 2/10 = 1/5, P(green) = 3/10, P(yellow) = 5/10 = 1/2. They add to 1." explain: > The **sample space** is the list of every possible outcome. If the outcomes are **equally likely**, $P(\text{event}) = \dfrac{\text{favourable outcomes}}{\text{total outcomes}}$, so $P(\text{even on a dice}) = \tfrac{3}{6} = \tfrac{1}{2}$. If they are not (a half-red spinner, a bag with more of one colour), use the sizes or the counts: $P(\text{red}) = \tfrac{1}{2}$. The probabilities of all the outcomes add to 1; 0 means impossible, 1 means certain. ```

# Kai's reasoning for the "find the mistake" task. Plain text: students click the wrong line, nothing runs.

# region: kai
The spinner has three colours: red, blue and green.
So the sample space is {red, blue, green}.
There are 3 outcomes, so each has probability 1/3.
# endregion
